Title: Zusammenfassend die Negativbewertungen…
Text:
Zusammenfassend die Negativbewertungen zu „Trustpilot“

Eine Geschäftsidee, wie man schnell zu Geld kommt bzw. Profit macht (ein TIP für jedermann):

- Man erstellt sich eine Website mit einen gut und seriös klingenden Namen, z.B. ist jetzt mal ein    fiktiver Sitename „Trusted-Copilot“.

- Dann erkauft man sich einen der obersten Plätze bei „Google“, „Bing“ und auch anderen Suchmaschinen und stellt sich im Web als ein seriöses und unabhängiges Bewertungsportal vor.

- Bietet Firmen und Shops ein Bewertungsportal, welches mit einem von mir eigens entworfenen Siegel (um unabhängig und seriös zu wirken), natürlich gegen entsprechende finanzielle Vergütung an. Somit kann sich eine Firma oder Shop wieder als „hervorragend“ im Web präsentieren, egal wie diese auf wirklich unabhängigen Portalen bewertet wird, um weiterhin Kunden zu täuschen und abzocken zu können. Beste Beispiele auf „Trustpilot“ sind „Opodo“ und „TotalAV“, sowie weitere unseriöse Firmen und Shops, die auf echten Bewertungsportalen keine Möglichkeit haben ihre Bewertungen zu manipulieren!

- Die Firma oder Shop, die oder der sich bei mir teuer einkauft verlangt im Gegenzug von mir, dass ich mich darum kümmere, die Shopsite von Negativbewertungen, auf verlangen sauber halte und positive Fake- bzw. gekaufte Bewertungen zulasse, was ich natürlich auch im eigenen kommerziellen Interesse selbstverständlich mache!

- Bei Löschungen von Negativerfahrungen und Anfragen von Bewertern kommen dann nur, wenn überhaupt, plumpe und nichtssagende vorgefertigteTextbausteine als Antwort, welche auf die eigentliche Problematik NICHT eingehen. Das heißt, echte Kundenerfahrungen sind mir egal, für mich ist nur wichtig das ich Profit mache!

Ein wirklich seriöses bzw. unabhängiges Bewertungsportal ist z.B. „Trusted-Shops“, da hat man echte und zuverlässige Kundenerfahrungen, sowie einen zuverlässigen KÄUFERSCHUTZ. Käuferschutz fehlt bei „Trustpilot“ um einigermaßen seriös zu wirken! Auf „Trusted-Shops“ werden keine Bewertungen, ob negativ oder positiv manipuliert, da kann jeder seine persönlichen Erfahrungen, die er mit Firmen oder Shops gemacht hat, OHNE ZENSUR veröffentlichen. Bei Recherchen zu Firmen oder Shops im Internet kann man sich da zu 100 Prozent darauf verlassen, dass es sich hier um ECHTE KUNDENERFAHRUNGEN, ob Positiv oder Negativ, handelt!

Title: Affidabile ma non troppo.
Text:
Affidabile ma non troppo.
Se le aziende recensite si lamentano delle recensioni negative, trustpilot le rimuove senza fare troppi complimenti. Mi è successo personalmente con un portale di trading che ha fatto rimuovere la mia recensione con due stelle. 
Trustpilot mi ha chiesto di fornire dati personali per dimostrare che ero effettivamente iscritto al portale recensito, io naturalmente ho rifiutato non potendomi fidare al 100% di truspilot né del portale di trading (eventuali ripicche?). 
Al posto loro avrei comunque lasciato la recensione, magari inserendo un avviso per i lettori (che so, qualcosa come 'recensione non verificata' o simili), invece loro hanno preferito rimuoverla del tutto. Improvvisamente il portale di trading in questione è passato da 2 stelle di media a quasi 4, poiché oltre alla mia recensione ne sono state eliminate decine in pochi giorni.
Immagino che ciò accada regolarmente con tutte le aziende che presentano reclami.
Non lo trovo professionale né corretto. A questo punto perché non chiedere conferme di identità anche per le recensioni positive? Non possono essere altrettanto fasulle?
Quindi ricordatevi che stiamo parlando di un servizio che tutela prima di tutto le aziende paganti.

I will be happy in "following up with" the privacy team, but if nonresponse/inaction continues these issues will be posted in boards like these to let others know.

Title: Rechtliches Verfahren in New York gegen Trustpilot welches vielerlei unseriöse Machenschaften offenlegt
Text:
Es sieht so aus, als wird Trustpilot schon bald juristisch das Handwerk gelegt, denn über eine 1-Stern-Bewertung in englischer Sprache habe ich nun erfahren, dass seit Februar 2021 ein gerichtliches Verfahren in New York gegen Trustpilot anhängig ist, welches ich auch im Internet finden konnte:

Trustpilot Damages, LLC v. Trustpilot Inc., Case No. 1:21-cv-00432, U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York

Dort heißt es, dass Trustpilot großen Unternehmen die Möglichkeit gibt, gegen Bezahlung bestimmte Funktionen zu nutzen, was man beispielsweise bei den hier schon kritisierten Fakebewertungen für Opodo sehen kann, wo ein Mohamed und ein Omar damit beauftragt wurden, massenweise 5-Sterne-Fakebewertungen rauszuhauen. Oder die Tatsache, dass die Deutsche Post/DHL ihr Ranking von stets einem Stern auf plötzlich 2 Sterne gebessert hat, seitdem diese gelangweilt ein und denselben Copy-Paste-Text als Antwort unter einer jeden negativen Bewertung hinhaut, obwohl dies nicht für einen guten Kundenservice spricht, denn es geht hier nur darum, damit das eigene Trustpilot-Ranking zu verbessern.

Im juristischen Verfahren wird jedoch beklagt, dass kleine und mittelständische Unternehmen, die ebenfalls viel Geld für einen Trustpilot-Business-Account hergeben müssen, nicht dieselben Funktionen erhalten, wie große Unternehmen, sondern sogar gar nichts, was bedeutet, dass allein der Meistbietende hier überhaupt etwas machen kann, während kleinere Unternehmen zwar bezahlen, jedoch für ihre Zahlungen null Leistung erhalten. Zugleich wird in der Anklageschrift die E-Mail-Adresse von Trustpilot, unter der man sich angeblich melden kann, in der Anklage als „Junk-Mail“ bezeichnet wird. Überhaupt betrieb Trustpilot, was seine E-Mail-Adressen anbelangt, hier wohl ordentlich Schindluder:

“But Trustpilot also owns “Trustpilot.net,” which hosts no website and is essentially a zombie domain. No Trustpilot subscriber would recognize an email from an address with “@trustpilot.net”—even if their email application didn’t block it as junk immediately. Yet, when Trustpilot faced a wave of subscriber cancellations on the back of its integrity scandal, it used “@trustpilot.net” addresses to send subscribers emails automatically re-enrolling them for another year’s subscription (and at higher rate). Subscribers did not see these emails originating from the zombie “Trustpilot.net” domain, and did not realize until seeing a new charge on their credit account that Trustpilot had secretly locked them in for yet another year. If they did complain, Trustpilot said it was too late to cancel.”

Ich denke, wenn ein Unternehmen, in diesem Fall Trustpilot, derartige Methoden nötig hat, dann sagt das eigentlich schon alles. Mal sehen, wie lange sich dieser Laden noch hält, doch es ist traurig, dass erst in den USA etwas zu dieser Sache passieren muss und die EU mal wieder schläft, anstatt dem offensichtlich illegalen Treiben eines Ladens auf dem Territorium eines EU-Mitgliedsstaates Einhalt zu gebieten.

Title: Eine Bewertung auf der Basis erlebter Erfahrungen bei Quora ist nur bei Trustpilot mit maximal 4000 Zeichen möglich!
Text:
Nachdem die Moderation von Quora keine sachliche Kritik duldet und mit unwahren Unterstellungen (z.B. Spam, unwahrer Behauptung einer Nichtverwendung des Klarnamens oder mehrfacher Verwendung unterschiedlicher Profile) "verbannte" Autoren mit der Löschung ihrer Beiträge schikaniert, die nach den Regeln von Quora das Eigentum der Autoren sind, bietet Trustpilot eine hervorragende Möglichkeit über erlittene Erfahrungen zu berichten, um gutgläubige Quora-Einsteiger über das ungeschriebene Waffenarsenal der Meinungsunterdrückung durch die deutschen Moderation (SP und JG) aufzuklären. 

Autoren sollten zur Wahrung ihrer Eigentumsrechte grundsätzlich ihre Quora- Beiträge und -Kommentare extern speichern, nachdem es überraschend zu willkürlichen und unbegründeten Löschungen gekommen ist. 

Mit Blick auf meine Quora-Erfahrungen Nr. 1-5 hat sich mein Eindruck verfestigt, dass Quora zum Nachteil regelwidrig verbannter Autoren, erheblich gegen übliche Compliance-Regeln verstößt. Der Begriff Compliance stammt aus dem Angloamerikanischen und bedeutet übersetzt so viel wie Rechtstreue bzw. Regelkonformität. Inhaltlich wird hierunter die Pflicht des Vorstandes verstanden, für die Einhaltung bindender Bestimmungen im Unternehmen Sorge zu tragen.

Schwerwiegend ist die Missachtung von Eigentumsrechten der Autoren an ihren Beiträgen, wenn diese - wie in meinem Fall - in Quora EN und DE vollständig gelöscht werden und eine beantragte Herausgabe meiner Beiträge (570 Quora DE und 750 in Quora EN) nach mehrfacher Aufforderung des Head of Marketing, Quora Northern Europe, Frau KE, verweigert wird. 

Die Missachtung dieser Eigentumsrechte ist ein vorsätzlicher Verstoß gegen das Quora-Regelwerk. 

Hinzukommt, dass die den Moderatoren gegenüber weisungsbefugte KE (Head of Marketing Quora Northern Europe) als Vorgesetzte der Mitarbeiter SP und JG offensichtlich nicht für die Herausgabe meiner Beiträge sorgt.

Title: Great concept, but lacks safeguards.
Text:
The concept is good, but I do not have any confidence that the platform cannot be manipulated by bad faith companies. 

Recently I noticed one company who have been reporting negative reviews which are then largely taken down. The nature of the complaints is the same and the reviewers diverse, but still they are deleted. 

My review went the same way despite attempting to reason with Trustpilot. 

At the same time as negative reviews are being purged, there is a clear case of mass posting of glowing, positive reviews (in one case over 100 reviews on a single day for a company that has just 300 reviews over the course of 4 years).

It's beyond suspicious, but any attempt to escalate this to Trustpilot is met with canned responses. 

How can anyone trust the veracity of company reviews when it's possible to turn an average review of 2* rating to 4.3* over the course of just two days?

In short, great idea, but lacking transparency and safeguards to ensure integrity of ratings.

Text:
I had posted a review of Parts Town in March of 2020, and today my review is not present on the Trustpilot web site, at all.  This particular review of which I speak is the only review that I had made on Trustpilot, until today at which time I make this complaint.  I was invited to post the review by Parts Town.

Parts town has over 14,000 reviews going back further than year 2015.  So how is it that my 1-star well stated review is disappeared from the entire internet?  The Way Back Machine's latest indexing of the particular company was 2019 - so there's no evidence of my activity, there.

Admittedly, the review was not a positive review overall (1-star).   I thought my review was concise, , well thought out (I made several drafts before publishing), and I spoke only of my own experience with the company, which to this day BTW, I still have a good relationship with.  

Trustpilot is a marketing service.  The reviews seem to be analyzed and weighed, and then sorted and culled to the benefit of the advertiser, according to my experience.

Trustpilot cannot be trusted, in my opinion.   Because my opinion, based on my true experience, was deleted.

RESPONSE TO TP RESPONSE:

I don't think that your software would have deleted it out of a case of fraud.  My post was reported to the company, and the company and I had extensive conversations about my comments.

If your software deleted my post on some kind of basis of fraud, this action only further strengthens my argument that Trustpilot manipulates the content to the satisfaction of it's clients - the companies that are advertising on the TP platform.

Because moderation is automated does not negate the end result of the automation - the removal of negative comments.  A human programmed the robot to operate within the objectives of the business, Trustpilot.

Title: Trustpilot verstößt selbst gegen die eigenen Richtlinien!
Text:
Auszug aus den Richtlinien:

Organische Bewertungen

Wenn Sie aus eigener Initiative eine Bewertung abgeben, nennen wir eine solche Bewertung „organisch“ – das heißt, wenn Sie sich bei Trustpilot einloggen und eine Bewertung zu einer Erfahrung abgeben, die Sie kürzlich mit einem Unternehmen gemacht haben, ohne dass das Unternehmen Sie zur Bewertungsabgabe eingeladen hat.
Wir haben bestimmte Regeln dafür, wer eine Bewertung abgeben kann und wer nicht.
Wann können Sie eine Bewertung abgeben?
Wie in unseren Richtlinien für Bewerter festgelegt, können Sie ein Unternehmen bewerten, wenn Sie kürzlich eine wirkliche Erfahrung mit ihm gemacht haben, z.B. indem Sie:

- etwas käuflich erworben haben,
 
- etwas bestellt haben (auch dann, wenn die Bestellung storniert wurde),
 
- per Telefon, E-Mail oder Online-Chat in Kontakt waren,
 
- ein Ladengeschäft besucht haben oder
 
- anderweitig die Produkte oder den Service des Unternehmens in Anspruch genommen haben.

Die folgende Negativerfahrung von Anfang Januar 2022 (mal wieder) im Auftrag von „TotalAV“ auf „Trustpilot“ gelöscht:

Kopie der Bewertung von Crystal

„Habe mich leider Dumm wie ich bin auf TrustPilot verlassen . Das war ein großer Fehler . A volte questo sito è l'unico modo per parlare con certe aziende. E almeno posso avvertire altre persone dei comportamenti scorretti o migliorabili di certe aziende.
Solo che molte aziende non hanno reclamato il proprio profilo, quindi non rispondono. Se una azienda riceve molte segnalazioni, magari è il caso di cercare di contattarli in modo più efficace che inviando un email a info@... indirizzo che non necessariamente è monitorato. Alcune aziende, tipo Amazon, hanno già numerosi profili in elenco e non mi viene permesso di aggiungere un nuovo sottodominio oppure in un'altra lingua.

Andando a leggere le recensioni degli altri utenti mi sono accorto che le lingue sono tutte mescolate. Quando scrivo una recensione vorrei poter indicare la lingua in cui la scrivo, così che quando vado a leggerle possa filtrare per lingua in cui sono scitte e/o Paese di provenienza. Il ricoscimento automatico della lingua non funziona tanto bene, infatti una mia recensione in italiano è stata catalogata come francese. E mi sono accorto che è possibile filtrare per lingua solo di recente, quel menù andrebbe evidenziato meglio.

Title: So here’s the deal.
Text:
So here’s the deal.

We've been using TP as our preferred review platform for the past 3 years.

We're a small business and have collected 250 reviews in that time.

We've always felt that the monthly subscription was expensive for us as an SMB but we liked the fact that we could use a widget on our website to display the latest reviews - so the £100 a month was fine.

A couple of months back I got a call from an account manager to tell me that the monthly subscription would be going up (100% in our case because we are apparently on a good deal). Additionally, for the extra money, we wouldn't be allowed to use the widget on our website unless we paid even more for that.

Does this business model work for anyone else? Our customers certainly wouldn’t appreciate a massive price hike combined with a service reduction.

I, for one, am not a massive fan of organisations that get too big for their breeches and think it's appropriate to reward customer loyalty in this manner.

Anyway, time to bid farewell to TP and stop promoting the brand on our website.

We're going to focus on collecting GOOGLE REVIEWS from now on. The payoff in terms of visibility in the SERPs seems to be of more value in the long run.

"Mr XXXXX, we have checked your evidence supplied and we can confirm that your reviews are 100% genuine and reinstated. Title: Trustpilot helped me to resolve an…
Text:
Trustpilot helped me to resolve an issue that I had with American Home Shield. I had reached out to that company 15x to get an issue resolved and was given scripted responses each time and they did not correct the problem. So, I went searching for other avenues and found Trustpilot!  After posting on Trustpilot I finally heard back from American Home Shield.  American Home Shield actually reached out to me instead of me having to call them which left me being put on hold so many times. Talk about wasting minutes of your life.  

I think so far Trustpilot is a great platform.  You can reach out and tell others your positive experiences with companies and also voice your concerns when companies are doing consumers wrong. So many companies are using artificial intelligence and customer service reps read generic scripts back.  It is so difficult to just get in touch with the person that can help you.  Trustpilot certainly helped me I am so grateful.  This platform is so necessary because feedback is important. Consumers are important.  We are not just commodities. Thank you Trustpilot.

Title: Misleading and unfair overall headline star ratings
Text:
The Truspilot headline star rating algorithm works in an unhelpful and misleading way. The headline star rating - the one everyone sees immediately and is instantly perceived as a reliable overview - does not fairly reflect any changing trend in performance and customer satisfaction, either upwards or downwards. 

This is particularly relevant where a company changes hands and its performance then either consistently improves or declines. Thus a company that has historically performed well but then later takes a dive and performs consistently badly still benefits from its historical good reviews, and a company that was performing badly but has changed hands and is now getting consistently excellent feedback is condemned to be blighted for years to come by those historical bad reviews.

The algorithm for this instantly visible headline star rating should be geared much more towards recent trends in performance, both upwards and downwards. Its weighting should be very steeply tapered chronologically, with very high weighting given to the most recent reviews, reducing exponentially down to zero consideration given to ratings received over 24 months ago.

Historical reviews and ratings may of course be important to some, and should therefore remain there for anyone to scroll down and see if interested, but these older reviews should not be reflected in that all-important overall headline star rating that most people use as an instant guide to current performance and customer satisfaction.

Title: Tyveri ved højlys dag :(
Text:
Vi blev kontaktet af Trustpilot i sommers, da de ønskede at lave en aftale med os. 

Vi vælger at indgå et samarbejde, da vi bliver lovet at:
1. Vi må anvende Trustpilots logo på vores webshop
2. Vi vil få vist vores stjerner i vores annoncer på Google Shopping, når vi blot har indsamlet 100 verificerede anmeldelse.

Efter vi har indsamlet 100 verificerede anmeldelser, kontakter jeg Trustpilot, da stjerne endnu ikke vises. De oplyser der kan gå op til 6 uger, før Google har registreret at man er berettiget til at få stjerne vist.

Efter 6 uger, vises stjernerne fortsat ikke, og vi kontakter igen Trustpilot. 
Vi bliver denne gang gjort opmærksom på at vi skal indsamle en anden slags anmeldelser (modsat hvad vi blev oplyst i første omgang). Vi står her foran vores højsæson og kan ikke nå at indsamle de nye anmeldelser, og beklager os til Trustpilot over at vi er blevet ført beg lyset. 
Trustpilot viser ingen forståelse el velvillighed til at finde en løsning.
Jeg har forståelse for at de har lavet en fejl, i og med de har lovet os noget, som ikke var sandt. Jeg er dog meget skuffet over at de ikke tager ansvar, men i stedet truer med inkasso.

Overvejer man at indgå en aftale med Trustpilot, vil jeg anbefale at holde sig langt væk.

Title: I order online both privately and…
Text:
I order online both privately and professionally - and I have an email address for private purchases and an email address for purchases for the company.
With my last review it happened that I was asked to review a purchase I made privately. The reminder went to my private email account, I quickly made the review, sent it - and then got a notification on my business account that the review was published under my business account!
I guess what happened was that I was still logged in with my business account and therefore the review that was supposed to happen with my private account got derailed and ended up on the business account. I don't like that, I'd like to keep private purchases and professional purchases separate.
I would like to ask you to cross-check the email address of the reminder with the email address of the currently logged in account. If there is a discrepancy - please do not just switch accounts! Ask the user if he wants to continue with the "wrong" account or switch to the "correct" one the email reminder went to.

Title: No support if a company retaliates for negative reviews
Text:
I have written a range of reviews and recently wrote a two-star review for one company. The director of that company then sent me five emails abusing me and calling me dishonest and a liar. He also replied to my review and posted my full name, which breached GDPR. 

When I sent Trustpilot his emails and complained about the sharing of my name, Trustpilot did not acknowledge my emails and have not responded at all, even though I contacted them three times. One month has passed and still silence. There was no protection for me at all and Trustpilot could not care less about the fact I was abused by the director. They also did not remove my full name from the director's libellous reply calling me dishonest, so they support GDPR breaches as well as breaches of their terms. I have waited for the statutory period to pass, and will now be reporting Trustpilot and that company to the ICO for a GDPR breach.

I have taken the time to share my reviews and develop Trustpilot's web content for free but there is no protection from retaliation from angry and aggressive directors, who try to bully reviewers for posting about their bad experiences. I would be careful when posting negative reviews on here, as Trustpilot will offer you no protection.

Title: I don't believe Trustpilot have robust…
Text:
I don't believe Trustpilot have robust enough measures to weed out fake positive reviews. 

My evidence for this is that two companies, GetaFlight and PH Travel, which operate out of the same address and under the same management, have vastly different reviews. The company respond to the many supposedly genuine good reviews for GetaFlight whilst completely ignoring the 82 out of 83 one-star reviews for PHTravel.

Many of the reviewers of PHTravel, mostly writing in over the past 6 months, claim that they have been DEFRAUDED. People often become emotional and make grand accusations when they feel badly treated, but in this case the charges appear to be genuine. PH Travel have repeatedly failed to return people's money for cancelled flights even when they themselves have received the refund from the airline. This is theft, and, by failing to properly screen the supposedly positive reviews for GetaFlight (which is the same company as PHTravel) TrustPIlot are in effect abetting this crime.

Title: Can Trustpilot be trusted?
Text:
I have been using Trustpilot, this website, for many years to get an impression of the service quality of other companies. Now however I notice that there's a significant number of reviews that look too good to be true when compared to other reviews about the same companies. 

When you see people who do lots of reviews here but never score less than 4 stars you start to suspect that they are being paid or compensated somehow for a positive review. I'm not sure anymore if Trustpilot reviews can be trusted. How can they identify fake reviews? 

(I left a one star review on Amazon not long ago for a faulty product that certainly didn't live up to expectations. Recently I was approached by the company making it by private email and later by the company email (after I insisted on that). They wanted me to remove my review or change it to a positive review in exchange for a refund. So clearly companies are giving people incentives for leaving a  positivereviewfora bad product or poor service)

Title: Trustpilot is open to abuse
Text:
Trustpilot is open to abuse. People can and do damage reputations and businesses with impunity. 
From first hand experience the Trustpilot complaints process is slow, laborious and self serving.
The response to this review will be a well written disclaimer, on how you can report problems, how they monitor and remove fake reviews however the reality is very different.
 
Within the time period it takes to carry out the review the damage is done. Malicious and vexatious content remains. I know of several businesses that have been targeted and nothing has been done to address their concerns or to remove the reviews. Only the business knows if the review is carried out by a genuine customer, please Trustpilot, tell me how you know the reviewer is a genuine customer? 

If you’re a business and you agree with my statement, please press like.

Title: Hallo an das Mitarbeiter*innen-Team von Trustpilot
Text: Bisher war ich als Rezensentin auf diesem Portal immer sehr aktiv. Verwunderlich ist lediglich, dass sich seit gestern das Zählwerk nicht mehr verändert hat. Ich habe den Eindruck, dass höchstwahrscheinlich Löschungen meines Accounts erfolgt sind, und ich somit völlig ohne Vorwarnung eliminiert worden bin. Wird mir von den Rezensierten ggf. etwas Rechtswidriges wie Beleidigung, Verleumdung oder gar Lügen unterstellt? Nein, ich kann hundertprozentig garantieren, dass all meine Beiträge der absoluten Realität entsprechen. Ebenfalls habe ich nach bestem Wissen und Gewissen all meine Kommentare gepostet sowie die Contenance gewahrt. Wenn ich einige Behörden und Unternehmen negativ bewertet habe, dann entspricht dies tatsächlich meinen Erfahrungen. Gehe ich recht in der Annahme, dass meine Vermutung stimmt? Ich erwarte Feedback bzw. dass alles wieder genau so veröffentlicht wird wie noch vor kurzem. Falls ich eventuell gegen  irgendwelche Richtlinien verstoßen haben sollte, dann ganz bestimmt nicht in böser Absicht. Offenbar gilt in diesem Kontext eingeschränkte Meinungsfreiheit. Einige schwerwiegenden Ärgernisse bestimmter Institutionen wurden von mir lediglich korrekt und ehrlich angeprangert. Zensur ist hierbei unangebracht, weil ich weder in meiner Ausdrucksweise ausfällig geworden bin, noch irgendwen bedroht habe. Gern erkläre ich mich bereit, einige meiner verfassten Beiträge zu bereinigen, damit sie wieder online für jeden ersichtlich sind. Eine Löschung zu veranlassen ist nicht gerade die feine englische Art.

Text:
I have now had all seven reviews of Hermes, posted in its Hermes UK Trustpilot profile, deemed "suspicious" and removed, some retrospectively, by Trustpilot's "advanced software". That includes a 5 star positive review praising Hermes CEO Martijn De Lange's office for resolving a problem when the company's customer services people had failed. "The last tracking event for a parcel that Hermes should have delivered on Friday 13 August told me that at 08:21 that day it was "on its way to the courier". But it didn't reach a courier and wasn't delivered. Neither was it delivered on Saturday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday or today. Additionally, a collection (a return not initiated by me) scheduled for today was missed. It appears that Hermes, having lost the generally reliable courier I had for eight years a few weeks ago, once again can find nobody to deliver or collect parcels in my area and undelivered parcels are piling up at the depot. It will be the fourth time this has happened with parcels previously delayed by up to twelve days."

The tracking number for the delayed parcel was provided to confirm the facts.

As a test, I have posted exactly the same review in the Hermes (without the 'UK') profile that Hermes hasn't claimed and makes no payments to Trustpilot for. That review is still there. If Trustpilot's "advanced software" is selectively removing reviews critical of Hermes from the Hermes UK profile that provides Trustpilot with income that needs explaining. Also, the transparency that Trustpilot claims it is committed to demands that it monitors the decisions made by the software and publishes the proportion of reviews of individual businesses it removes. Is that data available in the public domain?

Title: Trustpilot's rating can be mis-leading
Text:
I strongly disagree with Trustpilot's use of Bayesian Average whereby they automatically include the value of 7 reviews worth 3.5 stars each in all TrustScore calculations. This can give a totally mis-leading figure as per the following example.

I have just posted today a review of stay-zeni.com where I gave it a rating of one star (despite being sent an email confirming that my review is 'live', I still cannot see my review when I search for all reviews on that company - another reason for rating Trustpilot as poor!). The only other review - posted as recently as 6 days ago - was also a one-star review, yet the company receives an overall rating of 2.9 whereas the figure should be plainly just 1 star. If someone were to look solely at the overall figure, this would falsely represent the true performance of the company (you have to notice - and click on - the small encircled 'i' alongside the review stars to get information 
on Trustpilot automatically including the value of 7 reviews worth 3.5 stars) - something that not everyone will do.

Title: Super dårlig håndtering af Trustpilot!
Text:
Vores virksom har fået en uberettiget anmeldelse.
Anmeldelsen bør fjernes fordi, som Trustpilot skriver:
"Vi kan fjerne en anmeldelse, hvis brugeren ikke var berettiget til at skrive en anmeldelse af den pågældende virksomhed" - her er tale om en person, der intet har haft med vores virksomhed at gøre!
Alligevel fastholder Nick fra Trustpilot content integrity-team, at I ikke kan fjerne anmeldelsen!

I skriver videre:
#Hvornår kan du skrive en anmeldelse?
Ifølge vores retningslinjer for brugere kan du skrive en anmeldelse, hvis du har haft en reel oplevelse med en virksomhed inden for den seneste tid. Det kan f.eks. være, at:
    Du har købt noget.
    Du har bestilt noget (også selvom din ordre blev annulleret).
    Du har haft en telefonsamtale, e-mailkorrespondance eller online-chat med en medarbejder fra virksomheden.
    Du har besøgt en butik.
    Du på anden vis har benyttet virksomhedens produkter eller services.

Denne person har intet af ovennævnte gjort!

HVORFOR dette slagsmål med jer? :-/ 
Bør I ikke kende og følge jeres egne regler?

Svar til TRUSTPILOT:
Det er jo netop det, vi har gjort! Men medarbejderen har ikke læst, hvad vi har skrevet, og har efterfølgende ikke svaret når vi har forsøgt at udrede.
Det skal ikke tage 7-8 uger at få slettet en uberettiget anmeldelse - en anmeldelse I nu har slettet, dog uden at vi har fået de sidst svar fra jeres medarbejder.

Title: Not for small businesses
Text:
Trustpilot seems like a great place for small businesses to help build trust in their brands. Trustpilot has become a well known brand and it's where a lot of people go to read up on reviews.

Knowing this, Trustpilot have absolutely no hesitation in exploiting small businesses for hundreds of pounds each month to show reviews on their website, or even across social channels.

Despite Trustpilot not owning the user generated content (reviews) the Trustpilot team threatens small businesses with their "licensing department" should a business showcase any review obtained via Trustpilot without agreeing to their astronomical ongoing monthly fees.

The fees aren't as stated on the website, which is already too expensive for most grassroots companies getting off the ground, they're actually a lot higher once you get talking to one of their sales reps. Small businesses won't mind paying service fees, that's how things work, but they need to be affordable for small businesses.

If you're starting a small business, avoid Trustpilot, they can't be trusted to have your best interests at heart.

Title: Gut, könnte aber besser sein.
Text:
Finde es echt gut, leider gibt es aber einen Stern Abzug, weil man nicht sehen kann wie oft EINZELNE Bewertungen aufgerufen worden sind. Bisher sieht man ja ''nur'' auf dem Profil die Summe aller Aufrufe. Also gibt es so etwas wie einen Counter. Nur ist dieser anscheinend für Nutzer nicht zugreifbar.

Ich kann natürlich nicht für die Community sprechen, bin mir aber trotzdem sicher, dass ich nicht der Einzige bin, der bei dieser Möglichkeit eine höhere Beteiligungsmotivation hätte und dementsprechend aktiver hier teilnimmt bzw. bewertet und somit seine Impressionen mit uns teilt.

Vier Sterne dafür, dass die Bewertung der eigenen Plattform überhaupt erst möglich ist und auch auf Kritik geantwortet wird. Auch dafür, weil die Grundidee der Seite gut ist. Hinzu kommt einfache aber sehr schöne Gestaltung der Webseite. Mir missfällt, dass zu viele Unternehmen wissentlich die Bewertungen hier ignorieren und nicht auf die Kunden eingehen. Dafür kann aber Trustpolit logischerweise nichts, immerhin ist die Seite bekannt und es gibt einen sehr einfachen Prozess, wie sich Unternehmen verifizieren und vertreten können.
Sagt aber viel über die Beziehung zu den Kunden aus. Aber gut, das ist evtl. der falsche Platz für diese Worte. Wollte es aber trotzdem mal loswerden.

Ansonsten bitte halt nur meinen Vorschlag beachten, vielleicht lässt sich da was tun.

Danke im Voraus

Title: Fake reviews, horrible support and bots
Text:
Have been trying to get fake reviews removed for over a year and nothing happens.

We have tried everything - their messaging system, email, LinkedIn, long messages, short messages, honestly doing a handstand with a sign saying "please delete the reviews" was the only thing I have not done yet.

There is always something new, we reached the right team but clicked the wrong button, we try to flag but they have to check with the customer first, such a long and painful process. Honestly, you guys might as well hire me for your customer success team if your templates go missing because I know every single automated message by heart now.

And the funny thing is, there's 3 reviews talking about us trying to sell life insurance when we're a sales intelligence platform. Do you not think we have something better to do with our time than to prank call random people and pretend we are in a different business? You probably don't, as we waste so much of it writing to you even when you've proved time and again you do not care.

Do I expect to get this fixed? I honestly don't know. This is just to warn everyone to check other review sites before making a decision on the quality of a company, as many businesses like us will have their image trashed by bots like the ones you see here.

Maybe that explains why Trustpilot has so many bad reviews on Trustpilot. And Lord knows how many bots are writing their good ones. Because let's face it - if they can't recognise the bad reviews that are fake, would they recognise all the bots saying they're amazing and very trustworthy? And where do these undetectable bots come from anyway? No better way to find how beat the system than to be inside it, right?

Title: Pure, unacceptable greed
Text:
We've been with TrustPilot for quite a few years now, gathering reviews for our ecommerce site from customers who have purchased from us. We've gradually been offered more features at discounted prices which we've accepted.

However, over the last 3 years, whenever our contract is due for renewal, TrustPilot have tried to double or even triple the cost of our subscription. We are now constantly told that we should not be getting the additional features we currently have at the price we are paying.

This business model, whereby they give you all these features at an affordable price and then try to fleece significantly more money from you later down the line is absolutely disgusting.

We've now cancelled our subscription and downgraded to the free plan. TrustPilot have basically accepted losing a repeat, paying customer through shear greed.

In today’s current climate, with everything that is happening, that is a ridiculous company policy to have.

If you are considering signing up with these guys, I really would advise against it. You'll soon regret it in a a couple of years time.

Title: Lost Trust in Trust Pilot
Text:
I had a bad experience with a company that had a high Trustpilot rating. It was a company I hadn’t heard of but was reassured by their high Trustpilot score. 

I posted a review about my experience on Trustpilot, not wanting others to experience the hassle I had with the company. The company asked me to remove my review. Trustpilot then asked me to provide evidence of purchase (within 3 days) to confirm the validity of the review - which I did. I’m sure others wouldn’t be bothered, wouldn’t have time or would miss the email in this tight time frame. 

It seems that this approach (questioning bad reviews but not good reviews), is open for abuse and Trustpilot is facilitating unscrupulous companies in skewing their Trustpilot rating. 

For the transparency that Trustpilot claims, it would be useful if. 
1. The number (1-2 star) removed from a company rating is visible; 
2. The number of verified “good” reviews (4-5 star) are visible. e.g. where proof of purchase is requested, in a similar way to negative reviews.
3. Whether the company is paying Trustpilot, should be clear and visible. It would be interesting to know the difference in rating between companies that are paying Trustpilot for a service and those that aren’t.

Title: Wasted hours trying to log in
Text:
Wasted hours trying to log in as a reviewer. Initially forgot that I had previously opened an account: Every attempt to open an account assumed I was a business and I went round and round in a coding loop!

Eventually twigged that a new user would have to write a review first, then open an account as part of the process ..... ..... .... By some flook of programming, I suddenly found my review had been accepted. I did some brief editing and logged out. I received an email acknowledging my review, and used the link to access it. Then, keen to check how I had (by chance?) accessed my account ..... I tried to log in ...... another waste of time, while I tried to beat the password box, that only allowed two seconds before it timed out, and the password text was added to my email address box.

I am fairly confident I now have the correct email address and password to access my original account but when I try to login, the system goes round and round in a loop without explanation.

HELP !!

=============================

Response to the reply from Trustpilot

I asked for some help and gave a very detailed account of my experience, including my own mistakes. I was not expecting a reply. In fact, no reply would have probably been more useful. My hope was that my comments might have been forwarded to the website manager, in case my chance actions had uncovered a flaw in the programming. At no point did use the word "trust". I neither said, or implied, that I had lost "trust" in Trustpilot, however I'm now wondering how Trustpilot select the people they employ to respond to their reviews. I guess they would need to undestand plain English and have the ability to empathise with a customers experience and concerns before jumping to conclusions.

Title: Ancora non ci siamo!
Text:
19/01/2022
Faccio un uso estensivo di Trust Pilot, che, nel generale panorama di recensioni, mi sembra quello più serio; per cui ritengo di dover essere severo proprio quando recensisco Trust Pilot (e gli rendo merito di lasciarsi recensire).
Una delle mie critiche severe è quella dei casi di doppio dominio.
L'ultima recensione negativa su questo argomento risale al 14/05/2020 (Ticket 1401394).
In quell'occasione la risposta di Trust Pilot fu che la richiesta di unificazione la doveva fare l'Azienda.
Al che osservai che l'Azienda potrebbe non avere interesse a fare ciò, specialmente se uno dei due (o più) profili contenesse recensioni negative.
In seguito, ed evidentemente, Trust Pilot deve avere ripensata la sua politica ed accolto il mio suggerimento; tant'è che nella recente mia segnalazione di "doppio dominio" (non ricordavo di averne già fatta una) la richiesta di unificazione per il dominio di Regione Lombardia, è stata accolta (Ticket 1401394).
Dov'è, allora, il problema?
Il problema è che, invece di unificare i due domini, Trust Pilot ne ha eliminato uno senza importare nell'altro le recensioni; e guarda caso eliminando quello che di recensioni ne conteneva molte, peraltro negative, lasciando attivo l'altro, che di recensioni ne contiene solo una!
Poste Italiane ringrazierà sicuramente, ma ... a Trust Pilot devo togliere una stella dalle 2 che avevo dato in precedenza per lo stesso problema!

Title: Spero ne facciate tesoro per il bene di tutti
Text:
Trovo purtroppo poco efficiente il servizio di gestione delle recensioni e spiego il perchè:
Ho pubblicato delle recensioni da utente di un'azienda di cui usufruisco dei servizi mettendo Nome e Cognome in chiaro parlando di una esperienza reale come utente e rispettando tutte lo policy indicate e mi vengono puntualmente rimosse senza avere possibilità di capire il reale motivo.

Di contro non mi spiego come si riesca a dare spazio ad Heters che pubblicano recensioni palesemente false usando nomi di fantasia o identità rubate che nelle loro recensioni ci buttando dentro Falsità, Link vari a siti che monetizzano da pay per view,  insultano ed istigano all'odio , pubblicano dati personali con indirizzi di residenza e numeri di telefono di altre persone e violano tutte le vostre policy ! 
Non solo .... con copia ed incolla pubblicano la stessa recensione con lo stesso account più volte..... 

Mi chiedo è questo il modo di tutelare gli utenti e le aziende che si prodicano per dare il loro servizio ? 

Sono molto deluso dal vedere tutto questo ....

Ci sono grandi margini di miglioramento per dare un servizio realmente di tutela che potreste attuare ! Sopratutto in caso di palese attacco alla reputetion da parte di Haters che hanno come unico scopo quello di infangare l'azienda che recensiscono senza essere dei veri utenti ma sono mossi solo da interessi personali.

Vi proporrei nei casi di questo tipo di permettere recensioni solo da persone che possono dimostrare preventivamente il loro reale status di utente.

Esempio:
io faccio una mia libera recensione, ma se lo faccio per un'azienda sotto indagine chiedo di indicare Nome e cognome per esteso, e e-mail e numero di telefono di contatto (da non rendere pubblici ma solo per verifica interna delle identità) Solo dopo aver verificato che la recensione rispetta le policy indicate da Trustpilot ne autorizzo la pubblicazione Positiva o Negativa che sia.
In questo modo chi fa false dichiarazioni è rintracciabile in maniera univoca e l'azienda a prescindere con nome e cognome riesce a verificare se trattasi di utente reale o meno e rispondergli e dargli supporto se è in difficoltà. Inutile dire che non vedremmo più lo scempio che vediamo con recensioni piene di insulti e dati personali spiattellati in pubblico sapendo di passarla liscia senza risponderne penalmente perchè il profilo è falso e fatto da IP camuffato.

Che ne pensate amici di Trust Pilot ? Sto dicendo cose assurde ? Proviamo a migliorare tutto questo nell'interesse degli utenti ? 
O vogliamo lasciare liberi di fare danni agli Heters che sfruttano le vostre leggerezze per spargere fango e falsità protetti dall'anonimato ?

Ora sono curioso di sapere se rimuoverete anche questa recensione o se ne farete tesoro dei suggerimenti per migliorarvi.

Grazie 
Emanuele Bergamo

Title: TrustPilot - To the Moon!
Text:
Wat een geweldig bedrijf toch, dat Trustpilot. Wil superbelangrijke klantervaring verzamelen voor bedrijven en is daarin aardig succesvol. Cool, ik schrijf dus voor het winnende team!

En eerlijk is Trustpilot ook, want ik lees op de pagina van mijn belboer dat die betaalt voor informatie die ik over mezelf en mijn ervaring heb opgeschreven op het  'geclaimde' (dixit Trustpilot) profiel. 

Netjes, maar waarvoor betaalt mijn belboer dan? Ah, de betaalt-vermelding is een link, dus ik -click-. En dan ben ik op de corporate site van Trustpilot, alwaar  ik lees: 

"(...)Our business model - Trustpilot is free for everyone (...)" 

Gratis! Voor iedereen? Maar mijn belboer betaalt toch voor mijn data? Ofnie? 

Ik lees verder: "Anyone with a buying or service experience can write a review and any business can use our basic services completely free of charge (...)"

Nee, het staat er echt, bedrijven kunnen de Trustpilot  basisdiensten kompleet vrij van vordering gebruiken. Oooh, basisdiensten gratis gebruiken. Kompleet gratis zelfs... 

Maar daarvoor moet je die diensten wel eerst kopen, ja, nee, ok... Vandaar betaalt in die link. 

Je verwacht het niet en daarom hap je in dit verkoopgrapje. Van de dealer mag ik ook gratis in een auto rijden. Zolang ik mijn heilige koe maar wel eerst koop. Ja, ok... 

Nou is Trustpilot natuurlijk geen auto, meer een kompas waar hele volksstammen blind op varen. Als je goed bent voor vertrouwen, dan kan dat. Free zelfs. Free for everyone... 

Behalve voor bedrijven. Die moeten gewoon betalen voor een rondvlucht met de Trustpilot over die oceaan aan testimonals... Free for almost everyone, recht zo die gaat, mijn waarde TrustedPilot... ;-) Zeg dat dan gewoon, je hebt immers vertrouwen je produkt? Vertrouwen verkoopt zichzelf. Dan hoeft het verkopen van de prijs toch ook geen gegoochel te zijn? 

TrustPilot - To the Moon!

[En ook ik heb geen vergoeding of een andere beloning ontvangen om dit bedrijf te beoordelen. Beetje jammer eigenlijk wel, al zeg ik het eerlijk...]

Title: I'm updating my review…
Text:
I'm updating my review of the Trustpilot platform as I believe it is seriously flawed and easy for disreputable companies to manipultate.

Companies can report posts multiple times in an attempt to get them taken down. Where they flag them as 'harmful' then by simply reporting the post it is taken down to be reviewed.

Moreover it is possible for companies to just systematically report every report as false and Trustpilot takes that position as default and takes down reviews unless reviewers then decided to upload additional information containing the order. 

The problem here is two-fold. Firstly the assumption is that the company being reviewed is right and the onus is on the reviewer to upload additional information.

Secondly it's unrealisitic to expect that everyone will have the time or skills to dig out receipts and invoices and upload these to a third party website. That's assuming that they actually read or see the email asking for more information. 

So the very act of reporting every negative review as non-genuine will lead to at least a significant proportion of genuine reviews being taken offline. 

This is a massive advantage to unscrupulous reviewed companies and I've witnessed it being used to purge the majority of negative reviews posted for certain companies.

Title: Im Prinzip grossartig! - Kann aber nerven ...
Text:
Im Prinzip grossartig!

Allerdings, und das nervt mich furchtbar, wenn ich eine nicht so positive Bewertung abgebe, kann ich über die Bewertung vom Bewerteten kontaktiert werden. Beispiel: ich hatte eine Bewertung von 3 abgegeben, und wurde dann telephonisch kontaktiert, weil man effektiv unzufrieden mit dieser Bewertung war. Nach einem längeren Gespräch habe ich die Bewertung dann geändert (auf 4). Dann kann wiederum eine Mail von Trustpilot mit einer Antwort des Bewerteten.
Nun habe ich mehr zu tun, als über und wegen Trustpilot und meiner Bewertung fortlaufend kontaktiert zu werden. 
Wenn ich mit einem Anbieter kommunizieren will, kann ich das direkt tun. 
Wenn ich einen Anbieter bewerte, sollte es das im Prinzip gewesen sein. Ausser etwas wäre wirklich ganz falsch gelaufen; ein vollkommenes Missverständnis. So etwas lag hier nicht vor. Der Anbieter hatte selbst zugestanden, etwas nicht optimal gestaltet zu haben. 

Also werde ich zukünftig wohl keine Bewertungen auf Trustpilot mehr abgeben, weil ich daraus keine Dauerkommunikationsschleife habe möchte. 
Eine bewertung ist, meines Erachtens, immer ein Blitzlicht auf eine bestimmte Dienstleistung oder Ware.

Title: Spammer's Delight
Text:
Trustpilot used to be good but it's being abused by spammers posting referral links for gain which Trustpilot and others allow, condone and even encourage!

Companies like Smarty, Voxi etc operate referral reward schemes where the 'reviewer'/spammer is financially rewarded for every new referral/customer which results in certain people repeatedly spamming Trustpilot with reviews containing their personal referral links often multiple times per day and/or using multiple different usernames.

Reporting the spam to Trustpilot is pointless because they either approve the spam or ignore the reports thereby encouraging/condoning the abuser/spammer so it continues unabated.

Meanwhile the 'reviewed' companies gain new customers and often reply to the spammer thanking them and encouraging them to continue.

One spammer has openly boasted that they have 'recruited' over 250 new customers for one company purely by spamming Trustpilot!



Reply to Trustpilot.

If you do have customized detection software to detect fake reviews it doesn't work because it isn't detecting the spam/fake reviews.
If your Content Integrity team do actually look at the reported reviews they're either not doing their job properly or need re-training.

Text:
1.In The UK the identity of company directors is public information freely available from Companies' House. It makes no sense for Trustpilot to dictate that directors should not be named, thus permitting those directors to evade  being held responsible in a public forum for the action of the company. Trustpilot vaunts "transparency". This would appear to be a false claim.
2. Trustpilot should make prominent information as to how it is funded and in particular name which businesses have paid fees to Trustpilot and for what services. 
3. Trustpilot should publish information to show which, if any, positive and negative reviews have been subjected to verification and the outcome of such vetting.   
4. Businesses should not be given credit for "pro forma" responses to reviews. Before credit is given the reviewer should be asked if the business has actuakky taken any action to address the issues raised.

Title: Trustpilot. More bad practice.
Text:
Trustpilot are going to take down a review I posted on a plumbing company I had a very poor experience with nearly 2 yrs ago. I have shown them documentary proof of the transaction with this dreadful company so prooving that my review was based on a genuine experience. And yet they are demanding I send this company the job number and my name so that they can ''answer my problem more effectively''. This company had every opportunity to address my original complaint but chose not to do so, so they fully deserve the poor review and the negative comments that they have earned for themselves.      There are occasions when the behaviour of a company is so foul and aggressive that only an anonymous review, done to warn others, is safe. Allowing the  wayward company to identify the negative reviewer is unnecessarily dangerous and intimidating. This must stop!
It also is clear that Trustpilot is increasingly guilty of helping companies block reviewers they don't like from submitting perfectly honest negative reviews.
This episode then is a good example of how Trustpilot are fully complicit with rogue companies in manipulating scores to that company's advantage and of course justifies the additional fees paid by the company.
The other common practice is the tolerance by Trustpilot of multiple fake positive reviews which even a child could spot.
I think their 'Content integrity' team need to show a lot more integrity and stop supporting what amounts to criminal behaviour by these rogue companies.
No amount of denial by Trustpilot that they act fairly, equably or  that their fraud spotting technology is foolproof will convince me otherwise. The Trustpilot business model is badly flawed. Offering companies enhanced 'additional' services for cash creates a very serious conflict of interest which no one can deny. 
There are occasions when it would be great to have a 2-way conversation with Trustpilot even if it was only by e-mail. Trustpilot think they are so clever they can see all points of view without the need for anything being explained to them. They then arrogantly act as judge, jury, and executioner all in one!
Reading a company's 'organic' reviews  by clicking on the box to the right 'see a detailed overview' is still very revealing, (try it for Trustpilot for example), but reading most of the positive reviews, especially if added manually or by invitation is no better than reading fairy stories. I won't bother leaving anymore reviews good or bad on Trustpilot as they, predictably, have become more interested in profits than truth.

Title: Trustpilot har hævet 1.000.000,00 kr.
Text:
Trustpilot har hævet 1.000.000,00 kr. på mit betalingskort !!! Og de vil ikke betale dem tilbage :-(

Ovenstående påstand er naturligvis IKKE RIGTIG.
Men om anmeldelser er sande eller ej er ikke vigtigt her på Trustpilot. Det er man ligeglad med. Bare man skriver sin fantasi-påstand i en pæn tone.

Vi har hos Printerpatroner.dk været kunde hos Trustpilot i mange år. 

Sommetider modtager vores virksomhed dårlige anmeldelser fra vores kunder, som har haft en dårlig oplevelse. Nogle gange har de ret, andre gange mener vi, at de ikke har ret. Det kommer an på, hvordan man ser på tingene. En kunde har lov til at være uenige i vores forretningsgang.

Men nu har vi lige fået en anmeldelse fra en kunde, der påstår, at vi på hans betalingskort har hævet penge for en annulleret ordre, hvilket vi ikke har. Og han klager over, at vi ikke vil betale dem tilbage. Altså de penge, som vi aldrig har hævet.

Påstanden er DIREKTE USAND !

Her er altså ikke tale om, at han mener, vi har hævet penge, mens vi mener, at vi ikke har. Vi har IKKE på noget tidspunkt hævet et beløb.

Jeg klager til Trustpilot over den 1-stjernede anmeldelse, da der jo ikke er tale om en holdning eller oplevelse, men om SANDHED eller LØGN.

Trustpilot nægter at fjerne anmeldelsen, da de ikke vil tage stilling til, hvad der er rigtigt eller forkert. De kigger udelukkende på, om anmeldelsen er skrevet i en pæn tone.

Det vil sige, at man åbenbart kan skrive hvad som helst, man har lyst til.

Jeg har skrevet frem og tilbage med Trustpilot angående denne usande anmeldelse, men de holder fast i, at de ikke vil tage stilling til indholdet af anmeldelsen, men kun tonen.

Derfor denne anmeldelse.

Hilsen

Lars Lund
Printerpatroner.dk

Title: Algoritme werkt niet goed
Text:
Handig platform, maar de laatste tijd willekeurige verwijdering van beoordelingen. Het algoritme van trustpilot haalt wel zeer willekeurig beoordelingen weg. 

Zelfs een positieve beoordeling over een bedrijf, gebaseerd op mijn ervaring ermee, werd weggehaald. Pikant detail daarbij: het compliment was bijna woordelijk hetzelfde als een positieve beoordeling over een ander bedrijf, die wel mocht blijven staan.

Ook andere, eveneens gebaseerd op echte ervaringen, beoordelingen verdwijnen. 

Ik heb trustpilot al een paar keer gevraagd hoe dat zit, maar ze reageren gewoon niet. Nooit. Ook niet na een paar weken of maanden.

Op deze manier verliest het platform trustpilot steeds meer z'n waarde. Als ik geen echte, onafhankelijke beoordelingen meer mag plaatsen, zonder dat die willekeurig verwijderd kunnen worden, zonder enige uitleg, is de enige functie van het platform niet meer goed bruikbaar. Dat ondermijnt het hele bestaansrecht van Trustpilot, wat mij betreft.

---

Na de eerste reacctie hieronder:

De oplossing die in de reactie wordt gegeven, werkt niet. Dat heb ik elke keer geprobeerd, als er een werkelijke recensie is weggehaald. (Nu al twee of drie keer.) 

Ik krijg dan altijd een nietszeggend, copy-paste antwoord.  Dat biedt nooit een oplossing. Er wordt dan bijvoorbeeld naar onmogelijk bewojs gevraagd. (Dan moet ik bijvoorbeeld de kassabon van een nieuwssite, waar je gratis kunt reageren laten zien. Die bestaat natuurlijk niet.) 

Als ik vervolgens vraag om in te gaan op de echte vraag, krijg ik nooit meer antwoord. Zo wordt er niets opgelost.

Als je dus wilt dat ik een mailtje stuur, zou ik zeggen: check je mailbox. Daar staan die gevraagde mailtjes al. Dat heb ik al gedaan. Naar het genoemde e-mailadres. Maar daar kwam geen echt antwoord op. 

Oh ja, ik 'ervaar' dit niet zo. Er worden daadwerkelijk echte, werkelijke, geldige recensies verwijderd, zonder goede reden. Het algoritme werkt echt niet goed. Dat is geen 'ervaring'. Dat is een feit. En een fout. In het algoritme.

---

Na de tweede reactie hieronder:

Inmiddels is het opgelost. Aan de ene kant fijn dat het probleem is benoemd en ik de kans kreeg om het op te lossen. (Na maanden wachten op de kans om het op te lossen, moest ik opeens binnen drie dagen wat dingen doen; voelt een beetje ongelijk.) 

Aan de andere kant duurde het wel heel erg lang en veel moeite, voor ik antwoord kreeg op mijn vraag wat er mis was met spontaan verdwijnende recensies. Er werd meermaals niet gereageerd op berichten of er werd alleen een nietszeggend copy-paste-antwoord gestuurd en niet ingegaan op echte vragen. 

Over dat e-mailadres 

Ik heb een eigen domein, dus het kan dat het eerste deel van mijn e-mailadres (voor het @) een keer of wat is afgeweken van mijn officiële Trustpilot-e-mailadres. Dat was geen probleem bij het communiceren met de afdeling Content Integrity. Lijkt me geen reden om een negatieve recensie over jezelf dan maar meteen offline te halen. 

Vraag anders even aan de afdeling Content Integrity hoe het zit, daar heb ik contact mee gehad over deze kwestie. Twee of drie weken geleden zelfs nog met het e-mailadres dat ik zogenaamd sinds 2015 niet gebruikt zou hebben... (En alle andere bij-jullie-bekende e-mailadressen.) 

Al met al blijft mijn kritiek overeind, dat er zomaar reviews verdwenen, zonder opgave van redenen. Dat ik vaak contact hen moeten zoeken, om dit probleem op te lossen. Dat ik standaard alleen nietszeggende copy-paste-antwoorden kreeg, die helemaal niets verklaarden. Dat mijn opvolg-berichten (met vragen hoe dit probleem op te lossen) meermaals worden genegeerd. 

Dat zat hem niet in mijn e-mailadres. Dat zit toch echt bij trustpilot. Moeizaam, zou ik het hele proces willen noemen.
